take_homes: Put the context in a file the agent reads each session, so I don't retype it. For my team that means one shared file, not fourteen private copies.
The agent grades its own work too kindly. Use a fresh reader with only the output, and trust my own read of the subject over its report.
Name a framework I know, say how to tune it, and let the agent run it. Specific input gives specific output; vague input gives the average.

monday.move: Write a context file for the usage-pricing brief from the pilot-cohort data. Have the agent run it, then get a cold read from a fresh session before I send it to the working group.
monday.who: Me, then the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: If the cold reader finds nothing I didn't already know, I stop and don't build more.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files. Everyone would keep their own copy.

misconception.why: Phases 1 to 6 show the model stayed the same while the context changed. I still think prompts matter, but I now see that the file and the cold read matter more than clever wording.

one_line: Good on the context file and the cold-reader trick, but I spent an hour on a personal website and the dinner examples said the same thing three times.
